# teamcity_cloud_profile (Resource)

Manages a TeamCity cloud profile and the cloud images owned by that profile. TeamCity stores both as Project Features (`CloudProfile` and `CloudImage`), assigns their IDs, and links an image to its generated profile ID. The resource is suitable for an AWS EC2 profile whose image properties reference an AMI ID.

Cloud-profile properties can contain credentials or other secret material. The `properties` maps are sensitive in Terraform output, but their values still reside in Terraform state. Use an encrypted, access-controlled state backend and provide secrets through sensitive input variables or another secret-management mechanism.

TeamCity treats `secure:*` properties as write-only: their names can be returned without values. The provider preserves an already-configured secure value during refresh. After importing a resource, configure secure properties again so Terraform can apply them. Import IDs use `<project_id>/<cloud_profile_feature_id>`.

## AWS EC2 profile configuration

This resource is validated for TeamCity's `amazon` cloud provider. The provider-specific keys in the example are TeamCity AWS cloud-profile and cloud-image properties; select the values appropriate for the target TeamCity version and AWS account.

The resource creates one `CloudProfile` Project Feature and one Project Feature per `image` block. TeamCity assigns all feature IDs. Each image is linked to the generated profile ID automatically, so do not configure `profileId` yourself.

Image names are the stable keys used to reconcile nested image blocks and must be unique within a profile. Renaming an image creates a new TeamCity image feature and removes the old one. Changing `project_id` replaces the complete resource.

Use `TEAMCITY_HOST` and `TEAMCITY_TOKEN`, or configure the provider from sensitive variables, rather than committing a provider token. The example directory includes `terraform.tfvars.template`; copy it to an ignored `terraform.tfvars` only when a local value file is appropriate.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "aws_access_key_id" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "aws_secret_access_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "aws_ami_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "teamcity_cloud_profile" "aws" {
  name              = "AWS EC2 Build Agents"
  cloud_provider_id = "amazon"
  project_id        = "CloudAgents"

  properties = {
    "secure:access-id"  = var.aws_access_key_id
    "secure:secret-key" = var.aws_secret_access_key
    "region"            = "eu-west-1"
  }

  image {
    name = "Ubuntu build agent"
    properties = {
      "amazon-id"     = var.aws_ami_id
      "instance-type" = "t3.medium"
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

Import requires the TeamCity project ID and the server-assigned CloudProfile Project Feature ID:

```shell
terraform import teamcity_cloud_profile.aws CloudAgents/PROJECT_EXT_123
```

After import, add every required `secure:*` property to configuration and apply it. TeamCity does not return write-only secure values, so Terraform cannot reconstruct them during import. Use the TeamCity UI or the Project Features REST endpoint to identify the CloudProfile feature ID; do not use an AWS profile name as the import ID.

## State and secret handling

Both `properties` maps are sensitive because cloud profiles can carry credentials. This suppresses values in normal Terraform output, but values still reside in Terraform state. Use an encrypted, access-controlled backend and avoid committing `terraform.tfvars`, state files, access keys, or secret keys.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_provider_id` (String) The TeamCity cloud provider ID, for example `amazon`.
- `name` (String) The public cloud profile name displayed in TeamCity.
- `project_id` (String) The TeamCity project that owns the cloud profile. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `image` (Block List) Cloud images managed by this profile. Image names must be unique within the profile. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--image))
- `properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Cloud provider-specific properties. The complete map is sensitive because TeamCity cloud profiles can contain secure values.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The TeamCity cloud profile ID.

<a id="nestedblock--image"></a>
### Nested Schema for `image`

Required:

- `name` (String) The cloud image name displayed in TeamCity.

Optional:

- `agent_pool_id` (Number) The agent pool that receives agents started from this image.
- `properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Image-specific provider properties. The complete map is sensitive because it can contain secure values.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The TeamCity cloud image ID.
